question.text: If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>R</mi></math> is a function defined as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfenced><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{" separators="|"><mn>0</mn></mfenced></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is differentiable <math><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mfenced separators="|"><mn>27</mn></mfenced></math> is equal to (here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></math> represents the derivative of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi></math>)
